record.original_question: How should a distributed community manage membership so that participants are aware of the community and of one another, can join and leave appropriately, understand how they are expected to contribute, retain privacy for themselves and their data, and are introduced into the community's existing shared context when they become members?

evidence.quote: One aspect is thus the management of the community membership, which includes awareness of the community and individuals within the community, ways to join and leave the community, ways (or expectations) to contribute to the community, and respect for the privacy of individuals and their data in the community. Membership management must also introduce new community members to the existing context.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a distributed community modeled as a dynamic set of participants P(t) interacting over a peer-to-peer (non-centralized) communication network, together with a shared context state S(t) (e.g., shared documents, conventions, histories, or knowledge artifacts) that evolves over time. Design a membership-management protocol/framework that simultaneously satisfies all of the following requirements:

1. Awareness. Every current participant p ∈ P(t) can discover the existence of the community and obtain a verifiable view of the other current participants, despite the absence of a central directory.

2. Join and leave. There are well-defined mechanisms by which a new participant may join P(t) and by which an existing participant may leave, such that the resulting transitions are consistent across the views held by other participants under realistic network conditions (asynchrony, partitions, churn).

3. Contribution expectations. The protocol specifies, communicates, and (where appropriate) enforces the ways in which participants are expected to contribute to the community, so that each member has an unambiguous understanding of their role.

4. Privacy. Participants retain control over personal data and over data they generate within the community; the mechanisms used for awareness, join/leave, and contribution must not require disclosing information beyond what each participant explicitly authorizes.

5. Onboarding into shared context. When a participant joins at time t, there is a procedure that introduces them to a faithful and sufficient representation of S(t), enabling them to interact meaningfully with existing members.

Formulate such a protocol, give a precise model in which the five requirements can be stated, and either exhibit a construction satisfying all five simultaneously or prove an impossibility result delineating the achievable trade-offs.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open research challenge in the area of distributed/decentralized communities and has no known general solution; existing work on decentralized social networks, CRDTs, and access-control protocols addresses individual aspects but no unified framework simultaneously resolves awareness, join/leave consistency, contribution expectations, privacy, and shared-context onboarding.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in Distributed Communities
status_evidence.snippet: Membership management ... awareness ... ways to join and leave ... respect for the privacy ... introduce new community members to the existing context.
status_evidence.claim: The question is listed among open problems for distributed communities.
